She was defecating blood, and I thought it was quite serious, and I was right. She's been gone for a month now, and I was very upset. I don't know if they post reviews for the Muratella emergency room here.

I visited the shelter to bring blankets and food for the furry ones less fortunate than mine. I wanted to visit the shelter to understand the situation. The volunteer said there are 400 dogs inside. I must say that there was no smell, they were locked in cages, but they are allowed to go out in a small courtyard, separated from each other... I felt very sorry, but they are definitely not mistreated. I couldn't see them all, there are aggressive and sick ones that they don't let people see... From the fences I had read that it was a concentration camp, but honestly it didn't seem like it to me. The volunteers are also nice. Let's adopt these poor puppies of all ages... They give so much love.
I brought the blankets.
Well-run dog registry. I went last day for lunch, it wasn't crowded at all. I handled a dog transfer very quickly. Friendly staff. Clean facilities. Positive welcome.
I'm sad to read the negative reviews, but I'd like to ask you to please adopt them despite the staff's behavior. Our friends need a home and love even more. Thank you all.

I went this afternoon to the shelter on Via della Magliana
to see a dog who had recently been in the shelter since November 29th, registration number 2024/2034.
After filling out a 5-page questionnaire (not necessary because I just wanted to look at the dog), they told me I couldn't look at her because she was breastfeeding
her five puppies.
They could have posted on the website and said so when I called this morning. And what do they do after they're weaned? They're separated from their mother.

I won't add anything else.
